questions.scenario: Look at the diagram of a sundial seen from above at an angle. data.subject: Cambridge Primary Science 2 Learners Book PDF

findings.detail: 6 questions open with the same sentence (9, 11, 13, 16, 18, 22): "Describe how the length of the shadow changes from"

issues.label: 1a
issues.detail: Marking criteria allows both morning and evening as correct, but question asks 'Is it more likely to be midday or evening?' This phrasing suggests a binary choice between two options, not three. Ambiguity between question intent and marking criteria.
issues.correction: Clarify question: either ask 'Is it more likely to be midday, morning, or evening?' or revise marking criteria to reflect the binary choice presented.

issues.label: 2a
issues.detail: Marking criteria lists 2 marks but only describes content (correct time + explanation). No mark allocation specified (e.g., 1 mark each). Model answer gives 10:30 but diagram description says shadow 'near the lines for 10 and 11'—10:30 is reasonable but not explicitly justified.
issues.correction: Specify mark allocation: '1 mark for stating time between 10–11; 1 mark for explaining shadow position.' Clarify if 10:30 or 'between 10 and 11' is expected.

issues.label: 2b
issues.detail: Question asks about shadow length changes 'on a sundial' but model answer describes shadow length (which does change), not shadow direction/position (which rotates on a sundial). Conflates two different phenomena.
issues.correction: Revise question to: 'Describe how the shadow on a sundial moves throughout the day' OR revise model answer to clarify that shadow length also changes on a sundial as Sun's angle changes.

issues.label: 3a
issues.detail: Question 3a is identical to Question 1a (same context, same image, same question wording). Assessment repeats the same question with identical data.
issues.correction: Remove Question 3a or replace with distinct question (e.g., different time scenario or different phenomenon).

issues.label: 3b
issues.detail: Question 3b is identical to Question 1b (same context, same question wording about shadow length changes throughout day). Repeated question.
issues.correction: Remove Question 3b or replace with distinct question.

issues.label: 3c
issues.detail: Marking criteria item 2 reads 'Explanation of how the of the Sun affects shadow length' — incomplete text ('the of the Sun'). Appears to be corrupted/missing word.
issues.correction: Correct to: 'Explanation of how the angle of the Sun affects shadow length.'

issues.label: 4a
issues.detail: Marking criteria item 2 reads 'Explanation of how the of the Sun's affects the length of the shadow' — incomplete/corrupted text ('the of the Sun's'). Missing word.
issues.correction: Correct to: 'Explanation of how the angle of the Sun's rays affects the length of the shadow.'

issues.label: 6c
issues.detail: Question asks to 'State whether it is more likely to be morning, midday, or evening' but marking criteria only lists 2 marks. For a 3-option identification question, mark allocation is unclear.
issues.correction: Clarify: is this 1 mark for correct identification + 1 mark for brief justification? Specify mark breakdown.

issues.label: 8a
issues.detail: Marking criteria item 2 reads 'Mention of the of.' — incomplete/corrupted text. Missing word(s).
issues.correction: Correct to: 'Mention of the angle of sunlight' or similar.

issues.label: 9a
issues.detail: Marking criteria item 2 reads 'Explanation correctly states that the Sun is in the sky and.' — incomplete/corrupted text. Sentence fragment.
issues.correction: Correct to: 'Explanation correctly states that the Sun is lower in the sky during morning and evening.'

issues.label: 10a
issues.detail: Marking criteria item 3 reads 'Accept: the comes from a low / the are at a low.' — corrupted text with missing words ('the comes', 'the are').
issues.correction: Correct to: 'Accept: because the light comes from a low angle / the light rays are at a low angle.'

review.summary: Assessment contains 10 substantive issues: 2 repeated questions (1a/3a, 1b/3b), 5 corrupted marking criteria texts with missing words, 1 ambiguous question phrasing, 1 conflation of shadow length vs. position on sundial, and 1 unclear mark allocation. No factual errors in science content detected.
